title: A month playing trumpet with Louis Jordan
summary: When Jordan's trumpeter fell ill, Coridge Davis's manager sent Phillips to play a month, earning 50 dollars a night in one-nighters, ending in Atlanta.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: When did your brother, Clarence, play with Louis.
That must have been in the 30's.
Louis had a band of some sort?
Yeah, he had a band in El Dorado, Arkansas.
Oh yeah, I played with him...
When you were playing with Coridge Davis...
Yeah. The trumpet player got sick here...

Yeah. And Coridge asked the guy who was managing the band, named Vandenberg... He told me, 'Phil, how would you like to make about a month with Louis Jordan?' I said, 'Fine.' Because Louis Jordan was making some money then. You were getting $40 and $50 a night for one-nighters. The last one-nighter I played with him, I got fifty dollars, and he gave me fifty dollars. That was in Atlanta, Georgia -- my last night.
Bet you wanted to stay with him, huh?
Yeah, I would have liked to stay there. Easy playing. You didn't have no music to read.
